key_insight: Message-Passing Graph Persistence (MGP) integrates message passing into persistent homology to create graph descriptors that are provably more expressive than the PH-based descriptors it extends.
engineering_relevance: MGP offers a way to combine learned node representations with topological structure for graph classification and regression.
method: Update node embeddings using the current subgraph at each filtration step.
Associate updated embeddings with persistence events.
Use embeddings to select connected-component representatives while preserving graph-isomorphism invariance.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on an expressivity benchmark and several graph classification and regression datasets shows MGP outperforming other PH-based descriptors on most datasets.
watch_item: Updating embeddings at every filtration step may add computational overhead; the abstract does not quantify runtime or scalability.
